facts.text: ISO 6165 defines which machines count as earth-moving machinery, while ISO 20474 and its European twin EN 474 set general safety requirements for those machines.
facts.quote: ISO 6165 defines which machines count as earth-moving machinery, and ISO 20474 and its European twin EN 474 set the general safety requirements that every such machine must meet.

facts.text: ISO 6165 is a vocabulary standard that names and classifies earth-moving machines, including loaders, excavators, dozers, dumpers and graders.
facts.quote: ISO 6165 is a vocabulary standard that names and classifies earth-moving machines (loaders, excavators, dozers, dumpers, graders).

facts.text: ISO 21815-1, ISO 16001 and ISO 19014 apply to machines as defined in ISO 6165, so a mining machine's inclusion in ISO 6165 determines whether those standards apply.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-1, ISO 16001 and ISO 19014 all apply to "machines as defined in ISO 6165", so whether a mining machine is inside ISO 6165 decides which rules reach it [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 20474-1:2017 and its machine-specific Parts 2 to 15 provide baseline safety requirements for earth-moving machinery.
facts.quote: ISO 20474-1:2017 and its machine-specific Parts 2 to 15 give baseline safety requirements for earth-moving machinery.

facts.text: Collision avoidance is not the specialized purpose of ISO 20474's baseline safety requirements; ISO 20474 sits alongside ISO 21815 and ISO 19014 rather than serving as the acceptance standard for automatic braking.
facts.quote: Collision avoidance is not their specialized purpose; they sit alongside ISO 21815 and ISO 19014 rather than serving as the acceptance standard for automatic braking [Chapter 3].

facts.text: EN 474 is the European version of ISO 20474; its 2022 family includes EN 474-1 and machine-specific parts, and EN 474 is a machine-specific type-C standard.
facts.quote: EN 474 is the European version, in the 2022 family (EN 474-1 plus machine-specific parts), and is a machine-specific type-C standard [Chapter 3].

facts.text: In Great Britain, a notice dated 8 August 2026 listed the EN 474:2022 family as designated standards, giving a presumption of conformity under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
facts.quote: In Great Britain, a notice of 8 August 2026 listed the EN 474:2022 family as designated standards, giving a presumption of conformity under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008

facts.text: Designation of the EN 474:2022 family in Great Britain does not make EN 474 an automatic-braking performance matrix.
The booklet notes a small uncertainty about the number of the Great Britain notice dated 8 August 2026 that designated the EN 474:2022 family.
facts.quote: the booklet notes a small uncertainty about the notice number [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Whether EN 474 will be harmonized under the European Union's new Machinery Regulation was not verified because the list was still being prepared in 2026.
facts.quote: Whether EN 474 will be harmonized under the European Union's new Machinery Regulation was not verified, since the list was still being prepared in 2026 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Compliance with EN 474 will be part of a machine's declaration but does not establish automatic-braking performance; that evidence must come from ISO 21815, ISO 19014 and the safety case.
facts.quote: Compliance with EN 474 will be part of the machine's declaration but does not answer the automatic-braking question; that evidence must come from ISO 21815, ISO 19014 and the safety case [Chapter 3].

facts.text: A project spanning surface and underground machines must check which standards apply machine by machine because ISO 6165 determines scope.
facts.quote: ISO 6165 decides scope, so a project spanning surface and underground machines must check, machine by machine, which standards apply.
